---
title: "CrimeBusters: Victimisation Rates in New Zealand"
author: "Kaka-C"
output: html_document
---

Victimisation rates by age and sex for three crime types (assault, sexual
offences and theft from a person), using NZ Police unique-victim data for the
12-month periods ending June 2024, 2025 and 2026, and the Stats NZ mean
estimated resident population for the same years. See the technical supplement
for data sources and assumptions.

Required files in the working directory:

- `Data_Jun2024.csv`, `Data_Jun2025.csv`, `Data_Jun2026.csv` (NZ Police, "Age Sex ROV" dataset)
- `Population_data.csv` (Stats NZ, cleaned to columns `Year`, `Sex`, `Age`, `Population`)

Instructions on outputting to HTML:

Click the Knit icon (marked with a blue ball of yarn) on the RStudio script editor toolbar, or use the shortcut Ctrl + Shift + K (Windows/Linux) or Cmd + Shift + K (Mac)

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Clean the victim data

```{r}
victim_raw <- paste0("Data_Jun", 2024:2026, ".csv") |>
  lapply(read.csv) |>
  bind_rows()

victims <- victim_raw |>
  mutate(
    # Year in which the 12-month period ends (e.g. "6/1/2024" -> 2024)
    Year = year(mdy(Year.Month)),
    Crime = case_when(
      ANZSOC.Division == "Assault" ~ "Assault",
      ANZSOC.Division == "Sexual Offences" ~ "Sexual Offences",
      ANZSOC.Group == "Theft from a person" ~ "Theft from person"
    )) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Crime),
    SEX %in% c("Female", "Male"),
    !Age.Group.5Yr.Band %in% c("Not Applicable", "Not Specified")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Match the Stats NZ age labels, e.g. "0 - 4 years inclusive" -> "0-4 Years"
    Age = str_replace(Age.Group.5Yr.Band,
                      "^(\\d+) - (\\d+) years inclusive$", "\\1-\\2 Years")
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, Sex = SEX, Age, Crime) |>
  summarise(Victims = sum(Victim.Count), .groups = "drop")
```

## Clean the population data

```{r}
# Police data tops out at "80 years or over", so combine the oldest Stats NZ bands
population <- read.csv("Population_data.csv") |>
  mutate(Age = if_else(Age %in% c("80-84 Years", "85-89 Years"),
                       "80 years or over", Age)) |>
  group_by(Year, Sex, Age) |>
  summarise(Population = sum(Population), .groups = "drop")
```

## Join victims onto the population

Each crime type is left joined onto the population by year, sex and age.
Groups with no recorded victims have no match, so their victim count is set to 0.

```{r}
crimes <- c("Assault", "Sexual Offences", "Theft from person")

merged <- lapply(crimes, function(crime) {
  population |>
    left_join(
      victims |> filter(Crime == crime) |> select(-Crime),
      by = c("Year", "Sex", "Age")
    ) |>
    mutate(Victims = replace_na(Victims, 0))
})
names(merged) <- crimes
```

## Victimisation rates

Victim counts and population are summed over the three years (and over sex for
the age-only rates) before dividing, rather than averaging the yearly rates.

```{r}
victimisation_rate <- function(data, group_vars) {
  data |>
    group_by(across(all_of(group_vars))) |>
    summarise(Victims = sum(Victims), Population = sum(Population),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(
      Rate = Victims / Population * 100,
      Age = fct_reorder(Age, parse_number(Age))
    )
}

rates_age <- lapply(merged, victimisation_rate, group_vars = "Age")
rates_age_sex <- lapply(merged, victimisation_rate, group_vars = c("Age", "Sex"))

rates_age
rates_age_sex
```

## Plots

```{r}
plot_rate <- function(rates, title, by_sex = FALSE) {
  p <- if (by_sex) {
    ggplot(rates, aes(x = Age, y = Rate, fill = Sex)) +
      geom_col(color = "black", position = "dodge")
  } else {
    ggplot(rates, aes(x = Age, y = Rate)) +
      geom_col(color = "black", fill = "lightgray")
  }

  p +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = "Average Annual Rate based on 2024-2026 data",
      x = "Age Group",
      y = "Victimisation Rate (%)",
      fill = "Sex"
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}
```

### Plot 1: Assault by age group

```{r}
plot1_assault_age <- plot_rate(rates_age$Assault,
                               "Assault Victimisation Rate in NZ")
plot1_assault_age
ggsave("plot1_assault_age.png", plot1_assault_age, width = 8, height = 6)
```

### Plot 2: Assault by age group and sex

```{r}
plot2_assault_age_sex <- plot_rate(rates_age_sex$Assault,
                                   "Assault Victimisation Rate in NZ by Age and Sex",
                                   by_sex = TRUE)
plot2_assault_age_sex

```
